request.system: You are the brand sentinel, guarding a distinctive brand voice.
request.user:
Judge whether the copy matches the brand voice.
Voice guidelines: ['Write plainly and specifically; name the feature and what it does.', "Lead with the customer's trip, not the product's ego.", 'Prefer concrete numbers (weight, capacity, ratings) over adjectives.', "Respect the reader's experience; assume they know the outdoors.", 'Be honest about limits — say what the gear is not built for.', 'One clear call to action per message.']
Tone descriptors: ['grounded', 'practical', 'warm', 'understated', 'trail-tested', 'unpretentious']
Terms to avoid: ['guaranteed', 'miracle', 'risk-free', 'best ever', 'cure', '100% safe', 'unbreakable', 'lifetime warranty', 'revolutionary', "world's best", 'bulletproof']
Subject: 400 lumens. 40 hours. The Beacon is here.
Preview: Our brightest headlamp yet — built for the long nights out.
Body: Some trips ask more of your light than a quick summit push. A full night of route-finding, a pre-dawn alpine start, a multi-day traverse where you can't count on a recharge — those are the moments the Beacon was built for.

The Northbay Beacon puts out 400 lumens, the most of any headlamp we've made. At 95 grams, it won't shift your pack balance or fatigue your neck on a long haul. The 40-hour runtime means a single charge gets most people through several nights before they need to think about power again. When you do need to top it up, it's USB-C — the same cable that's likely already in your kit.

A note on what it is: the Beacon is a strong, practical trail and camp headlamp. It is not a climbing-specific or extreme cold-weather device, so match it to your use accordingly.

If your next trip involves any meaningful time in the dark, this is worth a look.
Score 0-1; a score below 0.75 is a fail.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose or code fences, of the form: {"score": <float 0-1>, "verdict": "pass"|"fail", "reasoning": "<one sentence>", "evidence": ["<short quote or fact>", ...]}.
